prov.text: ChoiceOne incurred a $900,000 provision for credit losses on loans during the third quarter of 2026, due to the increase in loan balances and $648,000 in net charge offs. The ratio of the allowance for credit losses to total loans (excluding loans held for sale) was 1.16% on September 30, 2026 compared to 1.16% and 1.18% on June 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025, respectively. Asset quality continues to remain strong, with annualized net loan charge-offs to average loans of 0.08% for the third quarter of 2026. Nonperforming loans to total loans (excluding loans held for sale) increased to 1.25% as of September 30, 2026 compared to 1.07% as of June 30, 2026. Notably, 0.40% of the nonperforming loans to total loans (excluding loans held for sale) is attributed to certain purchased loans which were identified prior to acquisition as having credit deterioration. Although nonperforming assets increased to $38.6 million at quarter end, the portfolio continues to benefit from meaningful credit protection. Approximately 35.5% of the loans are supported by SBA or USDA guarantees, and approximately 34.3% of nonperforming assets consist of residential real estate loans, where strong collateral values and ChoiceOne's historical loss experience have limited realized losses.

nonint.text: Noninterest expense for the three months ended September 30, 2026 increased $330,000 to $26.5 million, compared to the third quarter of 2025. The increase primarily reflected higher salaries and benefits and data processing expenses, partially offset by lower intangible amortization, occupancy and equipment expense, and lower other operating expenses. Compared with the second quarter of 2026, noninterest expense increased $494,000. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, noninterest expense decreased $9.0 million compared to the same period in 2025, primarily due to the absence of $17.4 million of merger-related expenses. Excluding those merger-related expenses, the year-over-year increase primarily reflected higher salaries and benefits and other operating costs associated with the Company’s expanded operations.

tax.text: Income tax expense was $3.2 million in the three months ended September 30, 2026 and $8.7 million in the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to income tax expense of $3.6 million and $3.1 million for the same periods in 2025. The tax expense for the nine months ended September 30, 2025 was reduced by the loss in the first quarter of 2025 due to expenses related to the Merger. The effective tax rate was 18.0% and 17.7% for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, respectively, compared to 19.9% and 17.8% for the same periods in 2025. ChoiceOne’s tax expense for the first nine months of 2026 was reduced by $600,000 as a result of purchasing a transferable tax credit that will be applied to 2026 income taxes. Depending on market conditions, management intends to purchase additional transferable tax credits in the remainder of 2026 to reduce tax expense.

net.text: ChoiceOne reported net income of $14.5 million, or $0.97 per diluted share, for the third quarter of 2026, and net income of $40.7 million, or $2.71 per diluted share, for the first nine months of 2026, compared with net income of $14.7 million, or $0.97 per diluted share, for the third quarter of 2025, and net income of $14.3 million, or $1.05 per diluted share, for the first nine months of 2025. For the nine months ended September 30, 2025, results were impacted by the Merger, which was completed during the first quarter of 2025. As of September 30, 2026, total assets were $4.5 billion, an increase of $162.2 million compared to September 30, 2025. The growth in total assets is primarily attributed to growth in core loans and warehouse mortgage advances.

ocf.text: Net cash provided by operating activities was $45.5 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $17.8 million for the same period in 2025. The increase was primarily attributable to higher net income and the absence of merger-related costs incurred during same period in the prior year and an increase in other liabilities for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same periods in the prior year.

intro.text: ChoiceOne Financial Services, Inc. is a financial holding company headquartered in Sparta, Michigan, with assets over $4 billion, and the parent corporation of ChoiceOne Bank. Member FDIC. ChoiceOne Bank operates 54 offices in West, Central and Southeast Michigan. ChoiceOne Bank offers insurance and investment products through its subsidiary, ChoiceOne Insurance Agencies, Inc. ChoiceOne Financial Services, Inc. common stock is quoted on the Nasdaq Capital Market under the symbol “COFS.” For more information, please visit Investor Relations at ChoiceOne’s website choiceone.bank.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Debt securities
lines.why: Bonds held for sale or to maturity: financial.

lines.name: Equity securities
lines.why: Shares held for their return: financial.

lines.name: Loans, net of the allowance
lines.why: Lending is a bank's business: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deposits
lines.why: Customers' money a bank holds is its business: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: On a consolidated basis, interest and fees on loans accounted for 76%, 64%, and 60% of total revenues in 2025, 2024, and 2023, respectively.
Interest on securities accounted for 12%, 19%, and 24% of total revenues in 2025, 2024, and 2023, respectively.
Major Customers: The Company does not have any single customer that accounts for 10 % or more of its total revenues.
The principal source of revenue for the Company and the Bank is interest and fees on loans.
The Company's primary source of funds available to pay dividends to shareholders is dividends paid to it by the Bank.

FDICIA sets forth the following five capital categories: “well-capitalized,” “adequately-capitalized,” “undercapitalized,” “significantly-undercapitalized” and “critically-undercapitalized.” A depository institution's capital category will depend upon how its capital levels compare with various relevant capital measures as established by regulation, which include a common equity Tier I risk-based capital ratio, a Tier 1 risk-based capital ratio, a total risk-based capital ratio and a leverage capital ratio.
The severity of the action depends upon the capital category in which the institution is placed.
The Company’s ability to raise additional capital will depend on conditions in the capital markets at that time, which are outside its control, and on its financial performance.
The Company depends upon the accuracy and completeness of information about customers.
In deciding whether to extend credit to customers, the Company relies on information provided to it by its customers, including financial statements and other financial information.
The Company may also rely on representations of customers as to the accuracy and completeness of that information and on reports of independent auditors on financial statements.
We rely on third party service providers for certain components of our business activity.
The Company relies on dividends from the Bank for most of its revenue.
These dividends are the principal source of funds to pay cash dividends on the Company’s common stock.
The earnings of the Bank have been the principal source of funds to pay cash dividends to shareholders.

The public trading market for the Company’s common stock depends on a marketplace of willing buyers and sellers at any given time, which in turn depends on factors outside of the Company’s control, including general economic and market conditions and the decisions of individual investors.

The Company cannot predict the amount, timing or nature of any future debt financings or stock offerings, and the decision of whether to incur debt or issue securities will depend on market conditions and other factors beyond the Company’s control.
ChoiceOne’s principal source of funds to pay cash dividends is the earnings and dividends paid by the Bank.
ChoiceOne’s accounting treatment for these loans depends on whether they exhibit significant credit deterioration since origination at the time of purchase.
The fair value of the collateral should be adjusted for estimated costs to sell if the repayment depends on the sale of the collateral.
